ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the quadrilateral is labeled P-Q-R-S, with P at the upper left, Q at the lower left, S above and slightly to the right, and R at the lower right. Side PQ is the left vertical side, PS is the upper horizontal side, QR is the lower horizontal side, and SR is the right slanted side. Diagonals PR and QS are drawn and intersect at a point, denoted as X. The number 10 in the figure is marked inside the left triangle PXQ, and the number 5 is marked inside the upper triangle PXS. Then reason: From the problem statement, P and Q are right angles, so PQ is perpendicular to both PS and QR; therefore PS ∥ QR. According to the method, set coordinates Q=(0,0), P=(0,h), S=(a,h), R=(b,0). Let X be the intersection point of QS and PR. On segment QS, the parameter of X is b/(a+b), so the coordinates of X are (ab/(a+b), hb/(a+b)). Triangle PXQ takes PQ as the base, with base length h, and the horizontal distance to X is ab/(a+b), so its area is hab/(2(a+b)). The figure gives [PXQ]=10, therefore hab/(2(a+b))=10. Triangle PXS takes PS as the base, with base length a, and the vertical distance from X to PS is h - hb/(a+b)=ha/(a+b), so its area is ha^2/(2(a+b)). The figure gives [PXS]=5, therefore ha^2/(2(a+b))=5. Dividing the two equations gives b/a=10/5=2, so b=2a. Thus from ha^2/(2(a+b))=5 we get ha^2/(2(3a))=5, namely ah/6=5, so ah=30. Quadrilateral PQRS is a trapezoid, and its area is ((PS+QR)·h)/2=((a+b)h)/2=(3ah)/2=45.

First describe the image: In the figure, the quadrilateral is labeled P-Q-R-S, with P at the upper left, Q at the lower left, S above and slightly to the right, and R at the lower right. Side PQ is the left vertical side, PS is the upper horizontal side, QR is the lower horizontal side, and SR is the right slanted side. Diagonals PR and QS are drawn and intersect at a point, denoted as X. The number 10 in the figure is marked inside the left triangle PXQ, and the number 5 is marked inside the upper triangle PXS.

Then reason: From the problem statement, P and Q are right angles, so PQ is perpendicular to both PS and QR; therefore PS ∥ QR. According to the method, set coordinates Q=(0,0), P=(0,h), S=(a,h), R=(b,0). Let X be the intersection point of QS and PR. On segment QS, the parameter of X is b/(a+b), so the coordinates of X are (ab/(a+b), hb/(a+b)).

Triangle PXQ takes PQ as the base, with base length h, and the horizontal distance to X is ab/(a+b), so its area is hab/(2(a+b)). The figure gives [PXQ]=10, therefore hab/(2(a+b))=10.

Triangle PXS takes PS as the base, with base length a, and the vertical distance from X to PS is h - hb/(a+b)=ha/(a+b), so its area is ha^2/(2(a+b)). The figure gives [PXS]=5, therefore ha^2/(2(a+b))=5.

Dividing the two equations gives b/a=10/5=2, so b=2a. Thus from ha^2/(2(a+b))=5 we get ha^2/(2(3a))=5, namely ah/6=5, so ah=30. Quadrilateral PQRS is a trapezoid, and its area is ((PS+QR)·h)/2=((a+b)h)/2=(3ah)/2=45.
